quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
Pass only on the right.
Watch for oncoming traffic.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the passing lane is clear.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check that the passing lane is clear. Use your turn signal to show other drivers you are changing lanes.

questions.question: Children under age ____ cannot sit in the front seat of a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Washington's Child Restraint Law requires all children under 13 to sit in the back seat. This protects them from injury in a crash.

questions.question: Before turning left, you must:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Let oncoming vehicles go first.
Move to the right side of your lane.
Wait for oncoming traffic to get a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let oncoming vehicles go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic light, you must let pedestrians and oncoming vehicles pass first.

questions.question: A blind spot is an area you:

options.text: Cannot see without turning your head.
Can see directly behind your vehicle.
Can see in your rearview mirror.
Can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas next to and behind your vehicle that you cannot see without turning your head. Check them before changing lanes.

questions.question: If you are driving slowly and cars are backing up behind you, you should:

options.text: Drive even slower.
Pull to the right and let other cars pass.
Do not let other cars pass you.
Turn on your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and let other cars pass.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than other traffic can be dangerous. If cars are backing up behind you on a two-lane road, pull off to the right and let them pass.

questions.question: A good defensive driver:

options.text: Always drives slowly.
Watches what other drivers are doing.
Drives at the same speed at all times.
Only drives in familiar places.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watches what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: A defensive driver watches for what other drivers might do and prepares for problems before they happen.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Driver mistakes
Bad weather
Poor road conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Driver mistakes
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers using signals to prevent crashes.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No U-turn allowed.
No left turn allowed.
No right turn allowed.
No turns allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A person signals you to stop.
There is a stop sign.
Red lights are flashing and gates are down.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop at railroad crossings when someone signals you to stop, when there is a stop sign, or when red lights are flashing and gates are down.

questions.question: ____ can reduce your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only high levels of alcohol can
Alcohol cannot
Any amount of alcohol can
Only alcohol levels above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Any amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your focus, awareness, judgment, and memory. It makes you a worse driver. Never drink and drive.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle coming, what should you do?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep moving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to emergency vehicles with lights or sirens. Move as far right as possible and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give them space to pass safely.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them space to pass safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down when someone wants to pass you. This gives them more room to complete the pass quickly and easily.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit on city and town streets unless a different speed is posted?

options.text: 15 mph
25 mph
30 mph
40 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph
questions.explanation: The default speed limit in cities and towns is 25 mph unless posted otherwise.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast in wet conditions. Driving slower reduces the risk.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of them quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. They have less protection than cars. Passing too fast can push them off course.

questions.question: What does a posted speed limit show?

options.text: Only a suggested driving speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The maximum safe speed when conditions are good.
The maximum safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed when conditions are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. You may need to drive slower than the limit if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on crosswalks or in marked bicycle lanes. On the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Go through if no other cars are coming.
Keep going because you have the right of way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights warn of dangerous intersections. Treat them the same as stop signs.

questions.question: What must you do when you hear a fire engine siren behind you?

options.text: Slow down until it passes.
Turn on your flashers.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the curb or side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Curves ahead.
A divided highway is starting.
A divided highway is ending.
Bumps in the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: A divided highway is ending.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the divided highway ends ahead.

questions.question: When you merge into traffic, you should:

options.text: Leave a gap of about four seconds.
Wait until your lane ends and merge, even into a small gap.
Merge anytime, regardless of the gap.
Merge only when other drivers have stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a gap of about four seconds.
questions.explanation: You need a gap of about four seconds to merge safely. If you move into the middle of a four-second gap, both you and the car behind you will have a two-second following distance. You need a four-second gap when you change lanes, enter a road, or merge lanes.

questions.question: Drowsy drivers:

options.text: Should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
Can drive so poorly they may look like drunk drivers.
Can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
Are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can drive so poorly they may look like drunk drivers.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can perform so badly that they seem drunk. Opening a window, playing loud music, or drinking coffee does not make a drowsy driver alert to road hazards.

questions.question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person get over the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning, you should:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Make sure your tires are properly inflated.
Slow down when driving in rain.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, make sure your tires have good tread and are inflated correctly. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at higher speeds.

questions.question: If your wheels drop onto the road shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the road.
Stop your car at the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the road.
questions.explanation: If your wheels drop onto the shoulder, reduce your speed without braking. Then carefully turn back onto the road. Watch for traffic when you return to the road.
